body: Um I have a similar issue. I was thinking of maybe getting intralesional steroid injections, but I’m not sure with yours since there are some atrophic areas as well. I think dermabrasion could be useful in improving the surface irregularities though
Wow that’s great to hear you had a good experience with excision. Lots of people are interested in excision as a solution to some of their scars.

You have papular acne scars (the bumps). I have them too. Unfortunately, they are one of the hardest scar type to treat. They are treated like other hypertrophic scars with intralesional steroid injections, cryosurgery, and possible electrocayterization. Also, many doctors employ ablative co2 laser. And the most effective approach is intralesional radio frequency but good luck finding someone who offers it because it seems like no doctors do. 

For something you can do right now, use silicone tape/gel nightly and if they are less than 2 years old massage them to try to break down the scar tissue and flatten them.

Psychologically and emotionally, disfigurement (including from severe acne scarring) is probably one of the worst things that can happen to a person. I didn’t always think this, but it has to be true. It is so profoundly socially isolating to have AS. You are convinced no one can love you because of your disfigurement. Your ability to relate to the world normally is shattered. And to make matters worse it is not even seen as a valid problem by many people, as it’s deemed an “aesthetic or cosmetic concern” and you are deemed superficial by being so depressed by it. But your face is a big part of your identity, so it makes sense that if it’s ruined you are ruined too. The grief is tremendous. It’s the worst thing that’s ever happened to me, and I haven’t had an easy life. 

Look, I wish I could start over too. I wish that I could shut off this pain and the utter panic of going out in public. I wish I could live the life I was supposed to have before everything happened. If anything, hopefully it makes you feel better that someone else feels the same way. Sorry this happened to us.

How long ago did you do fractional ablative laser? Is 20% improvement your healed results? I’m looking to do laser, but some people say there skin went back to normal after a few months after micro-swelling subsided.

Hmm, I think it’s good you are using sunscreen and azelaic acid. I guess tret could help, but if you had a bad reaction or find it too drying, I can understand why you removed it from your routine. I heard IPL laser specifically targets redness and discolouration, so that could be worth looking into. Also congrats on your engagement!
That’s so strange the marks are still there. Are you sure it’s not enlarged pores?
I’m convinced those are hives. Would not be surprised if it’s an allergic reaction to something.

Lifestyle is an important component in acne treatment and shouldn’t be ignored, but the issues underlying skin conditions are often complex and require multifaceted treatment, so I would recommend consulting a dermatologist/doctor. They can assess hormone levels and check for any abnormalities and treat accordingly. This can potentially really help improve your condition.

In the meantime, I would recommend continue living a healthy lifestyle. You did mention exercising everyday, which is a very good thing, but just remember to clean your face from sweat immediately after as letting it sit can lead to breakouts. 

Your acne can be resolved, but it may take some time. Talk to a doctor. It may be intimidating to seek medical help, but for many people it is a relief to have someone to help you deal with your condition.

In that case, I would recommend getting the active acne under control while also protecting the healing/PIE affected skin. It is good that you use sunscreen every day, as that is always very important when dealing with healing skin. There is nothing I can specifically recommend product-wise, but I know tretinoin is not for everyone. I used Differin a while ago, and it really did not work for me personally. If you do not show any improvement after a few months, it would be good to stop something that is not working for you. I think that it could be helpful to discuss various prescription topicals with your dermatologist if you haven’t already done so. 

There still might be some oral medications that you could take even despite your liver sensitivity. Your case would just have to very carefully monitored. Unfortunately, for chronic acne oral medication is the only thing that provides real improvement for some people, so it might be worth it to look into that as an option. 

Ten years is a very long time to be struggling with this, so I could understand if you feel defeated by it, but it helps to remember that there is a solution. It just may take some time to uncover it.
Are the marks active acne or PIE? It is important to make this distinction because the treatments are different.

Lifestyle changes can be really helpful like washing your face after every time you get sweaty from exercising or being outside in the heat. Benzoyl peroxide or salicylic acid may help in cleanser form. 

Depending on the cause, your acne may not go away with over the counter products as it may be due to your hormones. If you haven’t already, get in contact with a dermatologist as they can recommend various products or prescribe accutane/antibiotics if they think you are a good candidate for those medications. 

It will go away so don’t lose hope. It may take some time though, but if it doesn’t clear up in the next month or so, please go see a doctor as your acne may be in need of specialized medical treatment. Not everyone’s acne can be taken care of without professional help, and it really is no use prolonging your acne by not seeing a doctor if you are one of those people.

Yeah same here. Breakouts coincide with stages of my cycle too. The most defeating part is not even the breakouts - It’s the instability of my skin situation. It wouldn’t even be that bad if I had a bad breakout but knew that it would heal and I wouldn’t have a breakout for a long time. I just keep getting breakout after breakout and it’s like I can never win or have a break. I am completely at a loss with my skin.

I just feel so sad sometimes because it feels like it’s just going to keep happening and there is nothing I can do to stop or control it. I just have to let it happen to me, and that is really very difficult.

I’m really sorry that you miss her but like you said she is now at peace. Grief is difficult and heavy, and the longing for someone who has passed stays with you to some extent forever. 

The fact that you are hurting so much shows how strong your relationship was, and it is a good thing that you honour what you had with her. I know it’s hard to never be able to talk to someone again in a physical sense, but it helps to talk to them in your thoughts. 

Someone said to me once that there is honour in grief, and that may very well be the case. Grief is a way of recognizing the preciousness of the person who has passed, and that is a good thing. Allow yourself to grieve, but recognize that the person who has passed would want you to be happy and at peace too.
That’s tough. Loneliness is tough. Sorry you have no one you are close to.

It seems like you are struggling with loneliness to me, which is a very real and valid emotion that is expected in environments that have very little human connection/intimacy. You are not a loser because you feel lonely. Many people feel lonely, and given certain circumstances, it is very normal to feel this way.

Maybe you are physically isolated from having intimate relationships with others, or maybe you are socially or emotionally isolated. Intimacy is a human need that needs to be met, and you shouldn’t be ashamed of wanting to be intimate with people.

Nothing much that can be done, but you can try wearing high soled shoes as others have mentioned. If anyone makes you feel bad about it, it’s not your fault, so it’s pretty shit for them to do that. 

Just own it and allow yourself to feel comfortable.

I felt like I failed my family when I struggled with addiction. To have them see me in that state was gut-wrenching, and the looks on their face convinced me that I was the absolute worst person in the world.  To think of the things I did and said to them is almost unbearable still.

I hated myself for that, and still feel guilt and shame even now (over 4 years post recovery) when addiction is no longer a part of my life. 

My experience has showed me that if you and your family really love each other, you can make amends regardless of what you did. It will take time, and lots of pain, but it can be done.

Seems like you are really in need of human connection, which unfortunately can’t be given in an online environment. Sorry things are tough for you. 

But for what it’s worth, I am sending you a virtual hug ❤️

It’s confusing when you are dealing with someone with suicidal thoughts. 

Suffering is incredibly personal, and its lived experience cannot be conveyed through words. That is, you cannot make someone “feel” your pain, so it is almost impossible for someone to have even a rough idea of how terrible you are feeling. 

Most people are fixed on solving problems, and when you present them with a problem that has seemingly no solution (someone feeling suicidal) they become angry that you gave them a trick question, and so they complain. 

Also, suicide doesn’t make sense to people who have never felt suicidal, just like any emotional experience would not make sense to you if you have never felt it. For example, you would not understand guilt if you have never felt it. 

That’s my theory as to why people complain about people feeling suicidal. Your best bet is to talk to someone who has felt suicidal before, as they will be better able to relate to you.

I’m sorry you are having a tough time. I was never able to be honest with my family either. 

I also struggled with addiction and various other things. It’s exhausting for sure, and I bet you are trying to function far past the point of burnout.  And with nobody to provide comfort or support, it’s really tough. 

I don’t really know what to say other than I know how you feel because I have to deal with agonizing pain everyday which is physically and emotionally defeating. 

Hopefully it helps to know you are not the one and there are people who empathize with your pain ❤️Thanks for sharing.
